guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low, done_valid is assigned to 0.
When rst_ni is high and absorbed_o is in the true mubi4 state, done_valid is set to 1.
When rst_ni is high, absorbed_o is not true, and done_i is in the true mubi4 state, done_valid is cleared to 0.
When neither absorbed_o nor done_i are in the true mubi4 state, done_valid retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: absorbed_o and done_i must always carry a valid mubi4 encoding (either true or false encoding).
assumptions.risk: If an invalid mubi4 encoding appears, mubi4_test_true_strict will return false, causing done_valid to freeze and potentially stall the handshake indefinitely.

assumptions.claim: absorbed_o and done_i are not simultaneously in the true mubi4 state.
assumptions.risk: If both are true, done_valid is set to 1 (absorbed_o priority). This may violate protocol if done_i was expected to reset done_valid in that cycle.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni is asserted low for at least one clk_i cycle after power-up.
assumptions.risk: Without reset, done_valid initial state is unknown, leading to unpredictable handshake.

uncertain_points.claim: If absorbed_o or done_i receive an invalid mubi4 encoding, done_valid freezes (neither set nor cleared) and no error or alert is generated, potentially allowing a silent denial-of-service or data-dependent stall.
uncertain_points.cond: absorbed_o or done_i contains an invalid mubi4 pattern
uncertain_points.risk: State machine hang without detection, could be exploited or cause unrecoverable deadlock in security-critical padding path.

uncertain_points.claim: It is unclear whether the implicit priority of absorbed_o over done_i (line 800 vs 802) is intentional and safe; simultaneous true assertions might cause done_valid to be set when a reset was intended.
uncertain_points.risk: Potential protocol violation or unexpected done_valid pulse shape causing downstream misinterpretation.
